1.1.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Gunungkidul Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Gunungkidul.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Special Region of Yogyakarta.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Behavior Change Counseling is psychological counseling provided to male perpetrators of domestic violence to help stop violence and become a person who can respect their partner, so as to establish a better relationship with their partner and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
16. Networked Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as Networked P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Center in Gunungkidul Regency that organizes networked integrated services for women and children victims of violence, which is established by Decree of the Regent of Gunungkidul.
17. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence against Women and Children abbreviated as FPK2PA is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and established at the regency and sub-district levels.
18. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
19. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services, up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
22. Gender Mainstreaming in the Region is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
23. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions, and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
24. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
25. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women.
26. Disaggregated data is data disaggregated by sex and status and conditions of women and men in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
27. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting is a series of approaches to integrate gender perspectives in the planning and budgeting process, gender responsive planning is planning to achieve gender equality and justice, which is carried out through the integration of experiences, aspirations, needs, potentials, and problem solving of women and men.
28. Women and Children Supervision and Service Institution in Villages or Sub-Districts or by Other Names is an institution established by village communities that functions to serve victims of violence with members consisting of local community leaders.

Article 3

The purpose of protection of women and children victims of violence is to provide a reference for protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence in the domestic sphere and/or public sphere.

Article 26

1. Every person is obliged to prevent the occurrence of violence against women.
2. The Regional Government in efforts to prevent violence against women implements gender mainstreaming to realize gender equality and justice in the fields of education, economy, health, law, politics, religion, and socio-culture.
3. Gender mainstreaming as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out based on disaggregated data as insight-opening data in analyzing gender-responsive budgeting planning.
4. Further provisions regarding Gender Mainstreaming and Gender-Responsive Budgeting Planning shall be regulated in a Regent's Regulation.

Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:
a. threats of violence include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 4

The scope of protection of Victims includes prevention efforts, services to victims of violence, rehabilitation, and empowerment of victims of violence in the Region.

CHAPTER III

INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 12

1. PPT is established by the Regional Government, Vertical Agencies in the Region, or community institutions.
2. The Regional Government establishes a Networked P2TP2A as an integrated service center by Regent's Decree.
(3) The Networked P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2) is a functional work unit that has the duty and function of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
4. In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (3), the Networked P2TP2A may provide temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house.
5. In the event that the Networked P2TP2A does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (4), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION.

Article 37

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and child victims of violence, through Regional Work Units that have duties and functions in the field of women and child empowerment.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 27

1. The Regional Government and the community shall prevent violence against children.
2. Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the fulfillment of children's basic rights according to their needs.
3. Further regulation regarding the fulfillment of children's basic rights shall be regulated in a Regent's Regulation.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.

Point b What is meant by "justice" is a state where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access and welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Point c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Point d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER IV

EFFORTS TO PREVENT VIOLENCE AGAINST

WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

Efforts to Prevent Violence against Women

Article 20

The social rehabilitation service division as referred to in Article 13 paragraph (2) letter c has the duties of:
a. providing assistance during the case handling process; and
b. conducting counseling for victims and/or perpetrators of violence.

Article 25

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (5) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (6) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (7) What is meant by "other service units" is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence.

This service unit can be located in Integrated Service Centers (PPT) and Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT) based in Hospitals, Community Health Centers, Women and Children Service Units (UPPA), Trauma Center Shelters (RPTC), Children's Social Shelters (RPSA), BP4, and other religious institutions, prosecutors' offices, courts, Women Crisis Centers (WCC), and other similar institutions. These services can be in the form of one roof (one stop crisis center) or in the form of a network, depending on the needs in each region.

Paragraph (8) Sufficiently clear.

Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter (e) is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits whether material or immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

Article 32

1. The Regional Government implements empowerment for women victims of violence.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Networked P2TP2A and may cooperate with all parties.

Article 30

1. The Regional Government provides services to women victims of violence.
2. Services carried out by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by Networked P2TP2A, according to the type of service needed.

Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

Article 32

1. The Regional Government implements empowerment for women victims of violence.
2. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Networked P2TP2A and may cooperate with all parties.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Special Region of Yogyakarta.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Behavior Change Counseling is psychological counseling provided to male perpetrators of domestic violence to help stop violence and become a person who can respect their partner, so as to establish a better relationship with their partner and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
16. Networked Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as Networked P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Center in Gunungkidul Regency that organizes networked integrated services for women and children victims of violence, which is established by Decree of the Regent of Gunungkidul.
17. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence against Women and Children abbreviated as FPK2PA is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and established at the regency and sub-district levels.
18. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
19. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services, up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
22. Gender Mainstreaming in the Region is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
23. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions, and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
24. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
25. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women.
26. Disaggregated data is data disaggregated by sex and status and conditions of women and men in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
27. CONCERNING

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Gunungkidul Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Gunungkidul.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Special Region of Yogyakarta.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Behavior Change Counseling is psychological counseling provided to male perpetrators of domestic violence to help stop violence and become a person who can respect their partner, so as to establish a better relationship with their partner and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
16. Networked Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as Networked P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Center in Gunungkidul Regency that organizes networked integrated services for women and children victims of violence, which is established by Decree of the Regent of Gunungkidul.
17. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence against Women and Children abbreviated as FPK2PA is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and established at the regency and sub-district levels.
18. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
19. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services, up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
22. Gender Mainstreaming in the Region is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
23. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions, and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
24. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
25. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women.
26. Disaggregated data is data disaggregated by sex and status and conditions of women and men in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
27. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting is a series of approaches to integrate gender perspectives in the planning and budgeting process, gender responsive planning is planning to achieve gender equality and justice, which is carried out through the integration of experiences, aspirations, needs, potentials, and problem solving of women and men.
28. Women and Children Supervision and Service Institution in Villages or Sub-Districts or by Other Names is an institution established by village communities that functions to serve victims of violence with members consisting of local community leaders.

Article 4

The scope of protection of Victims includes prevention efforts, services to victims of violence, rehabilitation, and empowerment of victims of violence in the Region.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is Gunungkidul Regency.

2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of Gunungkidul.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Special Region of Yogyakarta.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against women and children will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Behavior Change Counseling is psychological counseling provided to male perpetrators of domestic violence to help stop violence and become a person who can respect their partner, so as to establish a better relationship with their partner and children.
15. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
16. Networked Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter referred to as Networked P2TP2A is an Integrated Service Center in Gunungkidul Regency that organizes networked integrated services for women and children victims of violence, which is established by Decree of the Regent of Gunungkidul.
17. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence against Women and Children abbreviated as FPK2PA is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and established at the regency and sub-district levels.
18. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
19. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, legal services, up to repatriation and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
22. Gender Mainstreaming in the Region is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
23. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions, and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
24. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and national security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.
25. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women.
26. Disaggregated data is data disaggregated by sex and status and conditions of women and men in all fields of development including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.
27. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting is a series of approaches to integrate gender perspectives in the planning and budgeting process, gender responsive planning is planning to achieve gender equality and justice, which is carried out through the integration of experiences, aspirations, needs, potentials, and problem solving of women and men.
28. Women and Children Supervision and Service Institution in Villages or Sub-Districts or by Other Names is an institution established by village communities that functions to serve victims of violence with members consisting of local community leaders.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION.

Article 37

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and child victims of violence, through Regional Work Units that have duties and functions in the field of women and child empowerment.
2. Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2

Point a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.

Point b What is meant by "justice" is a state where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access and welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Point c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Point d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Point e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of victims of violence to be able to work and earn a living independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GUNUNGKIDUL REGENCY NUMBER 25 OF 2012

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gunungkidul Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades their degree and human dignity, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Gunungkidul Regency.

Article 19

What is meant by "medico-legal" is medical services to provide optimal professional assistance in utilizing medical science for the purposes of law enforcement and justice. Medico-legal services include, among others: visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum.

What is meant by "visum et repertum" is a written statement made by a doctor in forensic medical science at the request of the authorized investigator regarding the results of medical examination of the victim based on their expertise and under oath, for the purposes of judicial proceedings.

What is meant by "visum et psikiatrikum" is a statement given by a Psychiatrist regarding the mental health condition of the victim that is needed to clarify a case and for the purposes of judicial proceedings.
